title: SD Guthrie closes FY24 on a strong note | The Star
text:
SD Guthrie closes FY24 on a strong note | The Star
KUALA LUMPUR: SD Guthrie Bhd , which recorded a near quadruple jump in its net profit to RM772mil in the fourth quarter ended Dec 31, 2024 (4Q24), remains positive on its prospects in 2025 and beyond, underpinned by strong support for crude palm oil (CPO) prices.
“We believe this year and even maybe to some extent next year, there will be other factors that come in and influence the industry’s supply and demand.
“We believe we are looking at a strong support for CPO prices this year and maybe part of next year,” said group managing director Datuk Mohamad Helmy Othman Basha yesterday.
He shared that palm oil prices had experienced a turnaround in 2024, leading to prices trading at a premium. Acknowledging that there might be factors that may lead to tweaks in terms of prices, he affirmed that “prices will be supported strongly”.
He added the biodiesel mandate in Indonesia and weather will play a big role in how prices will range moving forward.
Despite market uncertainties, Mohamad Helmy said positive prospects will bode well for the group’s performance.
This includes SD Guthrie’s entry into the Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone via a collaboration with AME Elite Consortium Bhd, Indonesia’s bullish stance on palm oil, and the huge potential for cross-border electricity exports to Singapore, as well as the China-Plus-One Strategy, which he said will help navigate geopolitics between the United States and China.
SD Guthrie saw its 4Q24 net profit nearly quadrupling to RM772mil, reflecting a basic earnings per share of 11.20 sen, compared with RM200mil in the same quarter of the previous year. Revenue dipped to RM5.26bil compared with RM5.28bil in 4Q23.
Closing financial year 2024 (FY24), the group’s net profit was RM2.16bil and its revenue stood at RM19.83bil. This was a jump of 7.61% year-on-year from FY23’s revenue of RM18.43bil.
The strong revenue for the year was driven by higher contributions from its downstream segment of RM17.95bil, while its upstream segment contributed to RM10.25bil across Malaysia, Indonesia and Papua New Guinea/Solomon Islands.
The group declared a full-year dividend of 16.36 sen per share, up by 1.36 sen from FY23’s total dividend.
As for its other business segments, namely, renewable energy and industrial development, Mohamad Helmy said he did not expect any significant contribution from the two segments any time soon.
SD Guthrie chief operating officer Mohd Haris Mohd Arshad said CPO prices are expected to range between RM4,700 and RM4,000 in FY25. “However, prices are expected to go down, probably after Ramadhan, and you will probably see the market trading towards the RM4,000 level, if not lower,” he said.
Mohd Haris said this expectation was considering the group’s view of which production will see good recovery in Indonesia and Papua New Guinea due to favourable weather conditions.
However, it was worth noting that the high production of soybean in Latin America may have a relative impact on palm oil value. “It does not make sense for palm oil to be priced at a premium if production is recovering. So, this will be quite bearish on prices,” Mohd Haris added.
When asked about the flooding in local plantations, he said Johor, Sabah and Sarawak were impacted, emphasising that it usually happened during low season.
“If the flooding happens around July to August, then we will have a problem. But as of now, our outlook for production in Malaysia remains unchanged,” he said.
